headline: Van Gerwen averages 103.83 to see off Wade 10-8
standfirst: Michael van Gerwen produced the highest average of the night and a four-leg burst from 7-5 down to beat James Wade and set up a quarter-final with Tom Sykes.
body: Michael van Gerwen beat James Wade 10-8 in the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts, and he did it with a four-leg burst from 7-5 down.

Wade led 7-5 after a 130 checkout and was finishing well. Van Gerwen replied with legs of 11, 12, 13 and 13 darts, two of them breaks of throw and one a 121 checkout, to turn the match round to 9-7. Wade hit back with another 130 to break, but Van Gerwen broke straight back to close it out.

His 103.83 average was the best of the four last-16 matches on Thursday and more than seven points above his 96.22 for the last 12 months. Wade was far from poor: 98.21, 42.1 per cent on his doubles and two 130 finishes.

The result fits a long pattern. These two had met 77 times before on the PDC’s records, and Van Gerwen had won 53 of them. Speaking to Dartsnews afterwards, he said Wade had tested his patience, but that he had answered “with the right arrows at the right moments”.
Van Gerwen, the 2017 champion, now plays Tom Sykes on Saturday at 7:15pm for a place in the semi-finals.
